classifiedFinding.title: phUSD mint authority is load-bearing for solvency; revocation, pause, or supply cap bricks claim/stake/withdraw without graceful degradation

classification.assetImpact: If phUSD revokes or pauses minting, all stakers with non-zero pendingPhUSD are locked out of claim/stake/withdraw. Recovery via pauseWithdraw (requires pauser cooperation) forfeits all accrued rewards.
attackPath: 1. phUSD governance invokes revokeAllMintPrivileges() OR pauses minting OR hits a supply cap.
2. Any user with pendingPhUSD > 0 calls claim/stake/withdraw.
4. Entire entrypoint reverts; user cannot exit normally.
5. Only escape is pauseWithdraw (forfeits all rewards) during a future pause.
classification.likelihood: medium — depends on cross-contract operational event at phUSD; phUSD has revokeAllMintPrivileges as a documented kill switch
classification.assumptions: phUSD sibling triggers a minting failure (revocation, pause, cap, or blacklist); KI-7 acknowledges the dependency but not the absence of graceful degradation
classification.externalRequirements: Sibling-contract action (governance of phUSD), not this owner

classifiedFinding.justification: Fits Medium criteria: protocol function impacted (DoS for any user with pending phUSD) AND value leak with stated assumptions (external requirement: sibling-side mint failure). Distinct from KI-7's configuration-requirement framing because the defect is the absence of try/catch / fallback. The trigger is a sibling-contract event, not this contract's owner — does NOT fall under the C4 'reckless admin' exclusion at this contract's owner level.
classifiedFinding.notes: Sanitizer flagged for review. Classifier keeps at Medium. The 'no graceful degradation' angle is the fresh defect, not the trust requirement itself. PoC: simulate phUSD.mint reverting and demonstrate the protocol becomes unusable.
